//: Medarx Phase 1 — Orthanc configuration. VERSIONED, NOT WIRED.
No Medarx component reads this file, nothing in the tree speaks DICOMweb,
and `docker compose -f infra/compose.yaml up -d` does not start this
container: the `orthanc` service is behind `profiles: ["orthanc"]` and
stays down until someone asks for it by name. It exists so that Phase 2
wires up a configuration that has been read rather than one assembled from
memory, and so the three DICOMweb gotchas below are written down next to
the file they will cost somebody an afternoon to rediscover.
GET /plugins  is the cheapest way to confirm the DICOMweb plugin loaded.
If /dicom-web is a 404 there, the image is jodogne/orthanc and not this one.
Name: Medarx-Phase1-Orthanc
// RemoteAccessAllowed: Orthanc ignores a key it does not know, silently. With the wrong key the
server starts, reports itself healthy, and answers every remote request with
401 — which reads exactly like an authentication problem and sends you to
look at credentials that were never the issue. This one cost a real
debugging session and it is the single most likely mistake anyone will make
In 1.10.1 (the version Debian bookworm ships, and the version this image
builds) remote access CANNOT be enabled without authentication. So this is
a Phase 2 decision that has not been made, not a Phase 1 setting: turning
it on is one way to expose a DICOM server to the network, and Phase 2 has to
decide how callers are authenticated before it does. It is left false here
because nothing in Phase 1 connects, and a DICOM server reachable from
another host is a finding in itself.
// Authentication: Left commented out on purpose. An `Authentication` block with a plain-text
user list is a credential in a tracked file, and Phase 1 has no user to
authenticate. Phase 2 sets this, and sets it from the environment.
// DicomWebServer plugin list: In Orthanc 1.10.1 the built-in REST API serves /dicom-web itself; the
`DicomWebServer` section below adds the *extra* routes on top, and naming a
module that does not exist is a startup failure rather than a no-op. The
DICOMweb routes are available as soon as orthanc-dicomweb is installed —
which is why the package is in the Dockerfile and why the two registry
images that lack it cannot be used.

// Logging: SystemFile and its level are left at Orthanc's defaults. A DICOM server's
log names studies, series and SOP instance UIDs, and every one of those is
an identifier; Phase 1 has no logging policy for DICOM traffic and inventing
one here would be inventing it badly. Phase 2 inherits the same
sensitive-data policy that `medarx.logging_filter` applies to Python logs.
